input: Audience: Wedding-business owners with established inquiry systems who are considering whether to make pricing, availability, location, or next steps easier to assess without a conversation. | Tension: Owners want to reduce repetitive inquiry work, but automation can be mistaken for a substitute for the personal attention some prospects still need. | Argument: A clear self-service path can let suitable prospects check practical fit questions before they need personal attention, while leaving room for the inquiries that require help. The useful design question is what couples can confidently assess on their own and where a human response still matters. | Take: Map the questions a couple needs answered before deciding to proceed, make reliable information available early where practical, and identify which cases still need a human conversation. | Mechanism: An elopement planner described a self-built flow that let prospects view pricing, availability, and locations and follow steps toward a quote. He reported that 80 to 90 percent of his customers moved through it easily, while he still spent substantial time with the remaining customers who needed more assistance. | Reader decision: Choose which fit questions your inquiry process can answer clearly without you, and define where a person should take over rather than assuming the system can handle every prospect.
